verdict.rationale: Honeycomb Triggers let users define threshold rules that automatically send alerts. Those alerts route to Slack, PagerDuty, Teams, or a custom webhook with templated JSON payloads, which can drive downstream actions, and triggers can be managed via API and MCP. However, the only automatic 'action' is alert or notification delivery on query-threshold or SLO-burn conditions; there is no native rule engine for arbitrary actions. Missing for 10: native non-notification actions (e.g., remediation or workflow steps), event-level rule matching beyond aggregate thresholds, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Use triggers to send alerts when thresholds that you define and configure are passed.
Set up Triggers and SLOs to alert your team when conditions are met, and route notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, or a custom webhook.
This allows you to build custom integrations that receive JSON payloads from Honeycomb upon alerts firing.
Route Honeycomb Trigger and SLO burn alerts to any service that accepts a JSON payload, including third-party tools and custom integrations.
